chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Abu Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Isḥaq ibn Shukr [Yashkur] al-Bahili, from al-Kahili, from Anas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever lights a lamp in one of the mosques of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, the angels and the bearers of the Throne will continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as the light of the lamp remains in that mosque.'

key_terms.أَسْرَجَ: Lit a lamp / placed a lamp

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for lighting a lamp in a mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* emphasizes the enduring spiritual merit of maintaining the physical environment of worship, linking the transient act of lighting a lamp to the continuous intercession of the angels and the bearers of the Throne (*Hamlat al-Arsh*). In Shia tradition, this underscores the concept of *Sadaqah Jariyah* (continuous charity), where the light serves as a tangible symbol of divine presence that sustains spiritual blessings as long as the illumination persists.
